label: adult-s3
summary: This network predicts the probability that a person earns at most 50K (training outcome rate 76%, training AUC 0.913). It is a logistic score made of twelve parts that add on the logit scale. The direct input edges carry most of the signal (switching them off drops the training AUC to 0.677): more education, being married to a civilian spouse, being a husband or wife, male sex, longer hours and capital loss each lower the predicted probability. Capital gain acts as a switch: in the typical case the probability falls from 64% just below the switch point to 4% a few thousand dollars above it, and the same unit also gives not-in-family people a fixed offset. Age matters below roughly the mean age, where younger people get a higher probability (90% for a young adult against 59% just above the hinge in the typical case), and barely above it. The other parts are category offsets (born in the United States, federal government, handlers or cleaners with an exception for Asian or Pacific Islander people, transport or moving, other relative, unmarried, El Salvador, a missing country or spouse absent) plus one dead unit. Two terms are fitted to tiny groups and push them to near-certain predictions: Scotland (16 rows) and without-pay work (17 rows).
